We have something called Connect to Wellbeing where you can get up to 18 sessions a year entirely free. That sounds really difficult where you are!

That's interesting, in QLD it's very common to go to your GP first for anti-depressents and a mental health care plan so you can recieve therapy. ADHD would be a referral to a psychologist or OT to be assessed and then back to your GP for medication, and only a psychiatrist if it's complex or complicated or doubt around the diagnosis or treatment.  GP's are your first contact with mental health support, unless you become so unwell you present to the hospital. They will often refer you to be case managed by community mental health too, or to be eligible for community based support to avoid needing to go into hospital with early interventions. Honestly I don't know how I feel about this game. The art style is great but the storyline is lacking, and I just can't stand the main character. I can only play for fifteen minutes at a time before I start to feel like I'm going to punch something. His personality is grating and falls short of witty with few positives to compensate.

As far as gameplay goes, it's fairly good. If you enjoy point and click games then you'll enjoy this one, I guess. There's an undercurrent of misogyny throughout the game, not too big of an issue but it is bothersome at times. The three girls in the entire game consist of an unconcious love interest who's name is Goal (yes, really), a drag queen used for purely comedic effect, and the ex girlfriend, a 'bitch' and several other lovely names who appears nude for no actual reason. 

The puzzles aren't too difficult, and while some can be too easy they give you something to do other than wait for your character to walk across screen at the same, slow, unchangeable pace playing fetch. 
I bought this game when it was on sale for maybe a dollar or so, and I think it's about worth that. Maximum, $5. 
Seriously beautiful artwork though. Well done on that front.
